skill.name: arm-cortex-expert
skill.description: Expert guidance for ARM Cortex-M firmware, peripheral drivers, interrupt safety, DMA coherency, and embedded debugging across common MCU families.
skill.summary: Build reliable ARM Cortex-M firmware and drivers with practical embedded systems guidance.

content.value_statement: ARM Cortex-M firmware often fails through timing, cache, or interrupt mistakes. This skill gives practical driver patterns and safety checks for reliable embedded code.
actual_capabilities: Designs peripheral drivers for I2C, SPI, UART, ADC, DAC, PWM, USB, CAN, and SDIO.
Explains Cortex-M7 memory barriers, DMA alignment, cache maintenance, and non-cacheable buffer placement.
Guides interrupt priority planning, critical sections, atomic state, and ISR-safe data sharing.
Compares Teensy, STM32, nRF52, and SAMD platform constraints for firmware design.
Provides debugging guidance for hardfaults, stack overflows, FPU latency, and peripheral address validation.
limitations: It provides guidance and generated firmware patterns, but cannot test code on physical hardware.
It depends on accurate board, MCU, clock, pin, and peripheral details from the user.
It references an implementation playbook that is not included in the scanned file structure.
It does not replace datasheet, errata, electrical safety, or certification review.

use_cases.title: Write a New Driver
use_cases.description: Create a complete driver structure with initialization, interrupts, buffers, and example usage for a specific Cortex-M board.

use_cases.title: Debug Timing Failures
use_cases.description: Analyze intermittent failures related to memory barriers, DMA cache coherency, interrupt priorities, or critical sections.

use_cases.title: Review Architecture Choices
use_cases.description: Compare HAL, bare-metal, RTOS, and Rust patterns for maintainable firmware across supported MCU families.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Driver
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a single peripheral driver.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design a Cortex-M driver for [peripheral] on [board or MCU]. Include initialization steps, interrupt flow, buffers, and safe defaults.

prompt_templates.title: Fix an Interrupt Issue
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Cortex-M interrupt behavior: [symptoms]. The MCU is [model]. Identify likely priority, shared-state, or timing problems.

prompt_templates.title: Plan DMA Safely
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced design for high-throughput data movement.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a DMA transfer strategy for [peripheral] on [Cortex-M7 board]. Cover alignment, cache maintenance, barriers, and validation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Firmware Architecture
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review before implementation or refactor.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this firmware architecture for [product]. Focus on driver layering, ISR safety, RTOS integration, fault handling, and maintainability risks.

output_examples.input: Design an SPI sensor driver for a Teensy 4.x project.
output_examples.output: A driver plan with transaction flow, chip-select timing, DMA considerations, cache alignment notes, and validation steps.

output_examples.input: My STM32H7 DMA buffer sometimes contains stale data.
output_examples.output: A diagnosis covering cache coherency, buffer alignment, invalidate timing, memory placement, and checks to confirm the fix.

output_examples.input: Review my critical section strategy for shared ISR state.
output_examples.output: A review of interrupt masking scope, atomic alternatives, priority effects, and recommendations for shorter protected regions.

best_practices: Provide the exact MCU, board, clock setup, peripheral pins, and SDK before asking for driver code.
Ask for validation steps, timing assumptions, and failure modes whenever firmware controls hardware.
Cross-check generated register usage against datasheets, errata, and vendor examples before deployment.
anti_patterns: Do not request generic embedded code without naming the MCU family and peripheral constraints.
Do not ignore DMA alignment, cache maintenance, or memory barriers on Cortex-M7 systems.
Do not deploy generated firmware to hardware without bench testing and fault handling review.

faq.question: Which platforms does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It focuses on Teensy 4.x, STM32 F4, STM32 F7, STM32 H7, nRF52, and SAMD Cortex-M devices.

faq.question: Can it generate complete firmware?
faq.answer: It can draft complete driver modules and examples, but hardware testing remains necessary.

faq.question: Does it support Rust embedded development?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes Rust guidance for critical sections, atomics, memory barriers, and safe shared state patterns.

faq.question: Can it debug hardfaults?
faq.answer: It can guide hardfault analysis using status registers, stack frames, invalid access checks, and platform limitations.

faq.question: Is this suitable for safety-critical products?
faq.answer: It can support design review, but it does not replace certified engineering, testing, or regulatory review.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the MCU, board, peripheral, SDK, clock tree, pins, timing needs, and observed failure behavior.
